body:
I looked into this.

For `x @ w`, AOT saves `permute(x)` for backward, not `x` itself. Eager `aten.permute` is a real view, so it shares `x`’s `version_counter_`. `x.add_(1)` between forward and backward bumps that counter and autograd raises, which is the point of the check.

Inductor does not emit `aten.permute`. It rebuilds the saved view with `_reinterpret_tensor`: new `TensorImpl`, same `Storage`, **new** version counter. After `x.add_(1)` you get `x._version == 1` and `saved._version == 0`, so the check never fires and backward uses the mutated values — the gradient of a forward that did not run. Same pattern for `bmm`, `einsum`, 3-D `F.linear`. Ops that save `x` itself (2-D `linear`, `mul`) still raise, which is why this looks operator-specific.

I would not share the version on every `_reinterpret_tensor` call. That helper is a hot path and is documented as view-tracking-disabled, like `unsafe_view`. AOT already rebuilds **user-visible** outputs that alias inputs with `gen_alias_from_base` in `runtime_wrappers.py`. Saved-for-backward views of a graph input should go through that same path so the saved tensor keeps `x`’s version.

Proposed approach
When a `SavedForBackwardsAOTOutput` aliases a graph input, regenerate it from that input with `gen_alias_from_base` (or equivalent version sharing only on graph-escaping views). Do not change `_reinterpret_tensor` globally.

Tests: compile `x @ w` (and `bmm` / `einsum` / 3-D `linear`), `x.add_(1)`, `backward()` — same `RuntimeError` as eager. Without the inplace, gradients still match.

I would be happy to raise a PR if assigned. Thanks!
